Framework Block defining one assembly instruction step. Document order in _steps
defines build order.

FunctionMapping translates between function-parameter lists and Capability inputType /
outputType. Concrete Mapping: org.blockml.bml.mapping.FunctionMapping.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language parameters
   (and reverse for returns)

Capabilities have no separate parameter list — only inputType / outputType. FunctionMapping
matters when a Capability is invoked as a function (built-ins, utility Sub-Blocks, expression
calls). Messaging transport ignores struct shape. Declared exception types live on
CapabilityDefinition.throws (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]) and are not part of
FunctionMapping.

Host-language return types in an implementation body (TypeScript number, string, boolean) are
FunctionMapping / host encodings of the BML outputType — not a second type system.
PrimitiveType.parseValue has outputType bml:Self; a TypeScript number for Integer is mapping,
not the Capability signature (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

inputType shapes:
• Primitive → single positional or named argument
• Named StructType / anonymous struct { a: Float, b: Float } → arity = field count; names =
  declaration order
• Collection field { values: T[0..n] } → exactly one positional sequence argument — not
  fixed-arity multi-arg expansion
Anonymous struct field types are full TypeExpressions — qualified references, multiplicity,
unions, and nested anonymous structs included ({ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer }). Arity
and named keys come from the field list; the field types themselves do not change the mapping
(doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes).

Nested collection inputType — for a grouped, nested multiplicity such as (core:ValueType[])[]
(doc:TypeExpressions — Nested multiplicities) the collection rule above applies to the outermost
collection. A positional/variadic function representation may therefore map each function
argument to one element of the outer collection:

  inputType="(core:ValueType[])[]"
  #lists.concat([1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"])  →  [[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]]

The inner collections stay ordinary typed values and are validated recursively against
core:ValueType[] — nesting changes the shape of the logical input value, not the mapping rules.

Canonical call forms normalize to the same logical input value (positional, named name=expr,
or object literal). Default FunctionMapping (when no explicit mapping is declared):
• Positional-only — arg i → field i in declaration order
• Named-only / object literal — keys = field names
• Mixed positional + named → BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS
• Too few / too many / unknown / duplicate → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS, BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER

Declaration order — same contract as ValueType instance configuration {…} positional args
(doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). This order is FunctionMapping at call sites, not a general
array-to-StructType conversion. Member access in expressions remains by name (point.x) —
not numeric index on StructTypes.

Custom FunctionMapping on an implementation may reorder/rename parameters or reject forms.
Required custom mapping absent → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING (reserved until custom mappings
ship). Ambiguous custom mapping → BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

Default mapping properties on mapping:FunctionMapping: supportsPositional=true,
supportsNamed=true, supportsMixed=false.

Generated Block Files come from the render target machineblocks-v3-scad
(@machineblocks/render-target). The CLI writes them under srcDir (default blocks).
This target does not emit a scad/user folder, a {root}.user package, online path
rewriting, or reserved submodule names help and func.

Manifestation. Automatic mapping replaces the single package segment bml with scad.
com.machineblocks.bml.examples.Cross becomes com.machineblocks.scad.examples.Cross,
module mb__com__machineblocks__scad__examples__Cross, and file
com/machineblocks/scad/examples/Cross.scad under srcDir. The class name is the file,
not an extra directory. Zero bml segments, or more than one, is an error unless both
source package and target package are set (--source-package and --target-package).
The compiled definition must sit in the source package. An equal package maps to the
target package alone; a longer name appends the tail. The header line Package is the
definition FQN (block.type), not the manifestation. settingsFormat must be absent or
"pseudo-map".

Header, first line exactly "MachineBlocks.com Block File", then Name, Filename,
Package, and Generated by. The target does not emit an FQN field, copyright, license,
or a visit line.

Section comments, in this order, with no "Mandatory Header" marker:
/* Imports */
/* Customization */
/* Main Module Call */
/* Main Module Definition */
/* Optional Sub Modules */
/* Optional Helper Modules */
/* Optional Global Functions */

Imports are posix-relative from the output file to {mbLibPath}/lib/block.scad (use)
and {mbLibPath}/config/mb_config.scad (include). mbLibPath is required. The CLI
takes config.mbLibPath, otherwise targetOptions.machineblocks-v3-scad.mbLibPath,
otherwise the directory of the installed @machineblocks/core package. There is no
fixed ../ depth and no rewrite to machineblocks/lib/block.scad or /mb_config.scad.
A Set also uses each placed type at its manifestation path under srcDir.

Which file is emitted:
• parts empty and presets non-empty → JSON, same path with .json. Shape
  { fileFormatVersion: "1", parameterSets }. Each set omits name, basePresets, values
  equal to that preset type's literal default, and values that do not serialize.
  Strings are stored unquoted; numbers and booleans are stored as text; a SizeXYZ
  value is stored as [x, y, z]. Presets are ignored when parts is not empty.
• parts empty and presets empty → error. Nothing is written.
• exactly one NativeBlock in parts → a leaf .scad file. The main call is mb_block
  at file scope. No wrapper module is emitted. Each NativeBlock parameter must be
  a property reference whose property has a literal default.
• any other parts list → a composite module mb__…(config = undef, settings = undef)
  that calls mb_block(base = false, studs = false) and one child mb_block per part.
• a Set → module mb__…(config = undef) with no settings parameter.
bml:each, bml:if, and bml:with are rejected.

Customizer lines on leaf and composite files are bare assignments, one per literal
property: name = value. serializeLiteral accepts a boolean, a number, a quoted string,
and a SizeXYZ {x, y, z} as [x, y, z]. The target emits no tab, no range comment,
no enum annotation, and no /* [Hidden] */ section. It does not apply grid step 0.25
or mbu step 0.125, and it does not clamp ranges to 32, 160, or 64.

The only customizer annotations this target emits are on a Set:
mode = "total"; // [total:Total, print:3D Print, step:Step, instance:Instance]
step = 0; // [0:9]
instanceId = the first placed id, or "00001" when nothing is placed
assembly = "merged"; // [unassembled:Unassembled, assembled:Assembled, merged:Merged]
baseColor = a string literal on the definition, otherwise "#EAC645"
The step range is the fixed comment [0:9], not the number of steps. Dispatch uses
mode, step, and instanceId. The generated set module does not read assembly or
baseColor. Print and total both call every instance module; neither calls
mb_set_step_print_position. The set wrapper sizes itself with mb_set_bounding_box,
which this library does not define.

A composite that does not declare size, and whose every part has a literal size,
emits parts = [[id, size, direction, offset], …] and size = mb_parts_total_size(parts).
Direction defaults to "west" and offset to [0, 0, 0]. That is why the size helper
reads size, direction, and offset at indexes 1, 2, and 3 (see HelperApi). A Set
writes the same four-slot row into STEPS.

Inside a composite module the config parameter is passed on. The file-level variable
mb_config is only the argument of the main call. Submodules, helper modules, and
global functions are comment placeholders, except on a Set, which fills Optional
Sub Modules with the module name plus __Total, __Print, __Step, __Instance,
and __Instance_{id}.

Generic parameters belong exclusively to the Block that declares them — never inherited
implicitly. When a generic Block is used as baseType, the derived Block must account for every
base parameter by either binding it to a concrete TypeExpression in baseType or forwarding it
to a parameter declared on the derived Block. All bound → concrete; any forwarded → remains
generic. Resolution runs during inheritance: bound parameters are substituted throughout the
inherited definition. Validator checks: every base parameter accounted for, argument count
matches, each bound argument satisfies the parameter baseType (satisfiesTypeBound), forwarded
parameters are declared locally.

Type-level binding uses baseType application: a derived Block must bind or forward every base
parameter (PrimitiveEntity(T) → IntegerEntity with baseType PrimitiveEntity(Integer), etc.).
Instance-level binding uses bml:generics. A type whose genericTypes remain open after inheritance
cannot appear as an aggregation child unless bml:generics binds those parameters. Abstract
Blocks remain uninstantiable even with bml:generics.

Declaration — on the Block via <genericTypes> (meta-model GenericTypeDefinition). Parameter
name = XML element local name (<T baseType="…"/>). Optional defaultType when an application
omits the argument:
1. Concrete TypeExpression (e.g. type:Decimal)
2. Earlier sibling parameter name only (declaration-order DAG; no forward refs/cycles)
Resolution: authored args win → unbound params get defaults in declaration order → every
parameter must ground to a concrete TypeExpression → each binding satisfies baseType.
Diagnostics: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_FORWARD_REF, BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_CYCLE,
BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_UNRESOLVED, BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

BML attribute syntax — round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block),
InstanceReference(core:Block), SelectiveGrid(Boolean | type:HoleType). Each (…) argument is a
TypeExpression. With multiple parameters, labels match generic parameter names. At validate
time placeholders (T) are substituted; mismatch → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

Instance syntax — bml:generics on the Block instance (attribute or child element). The value is
only the parenthesized argument list; the type name is the instance tag. Parentheses are
required. Same TypeExpression grammar as baseType arguments. Authored args win; remaining
parameters take defaultType in declaration order. After resolution every parameter must be
concrete. Incorrect: <MyBlock someProp="Value"/> when MyBlock still has open T. Correct:
<MyBlock bml:generics="(type:Integer)"/> or
<TestBlock><bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics></TestBlock>.
Open generic aggregated without the directive → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. bml:generics
anywhere other than a Block instance → BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Argument list
incompatible with the instance's open genericTypes → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. Missing
required argument with no defaultType → BML_MISSING_GENERIC_TYPE_ARGUMENT. Ill-formed
TypeExpression → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.

Orthogonal to {…} ValueType instance configuration (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration) and to
multiplicity brackets (doc:TypeExpressions).

Sub-Blocks / embeds may declare own genericTypes (Java static nested class model) — they do not
see enclosing generics; forward explicitly (Item(T)). Name collisions on the same declaring
Block with Block name or direct Sub-Block → BML_GENERIC_BLOCK_NAME_COLLISION /
BML_GENERIC_SUBBLOCK_NAME_COLLISION.

Constraint generics — Constraint branches declare genericTypes but arguments are never authored;
the compiler binds T from the <constraints> embedding context (Property → ValueType,
Aggregation → AggregationDefinition, Block → BlockDefinition, …). Branch ↔ context mismatch →
BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH. Validation property (Error/Warning/Information) controls
enforcement; omitted → metadata only.

Geometry and children are built first in local space, then transformed together. After the
local build, the effective order is:

direction → align → rotationOffset → rotation → rotationOffsetRevert → offset

direction — semantic 90° grid orientation (West / North / East / South). At North and South,
size X and Y swap for placement; face semantics stay west-local for authoring.
Prefer direction over free rotation whenever the intent is grid-aligned reorientation.
SCAD serialize literals (scad:value): west / north / east / south.

align — Start / Center / End relative to the reference bounding box (studs, slope, bevel, and
baseCrop do not change the align box). Scalar Align may broadcast, or AxisXYZ(Align) sets each
axis. alignChildren sets the parent origin used by children (default Start on all axes).
SCAD serialize literals (scad:value): start / center / end.

rotation — free rotation after alignment; not grid-safe; last resort.
rotationOffset — optional pivot for rotation; may be reverted after rotation.
offset — final placement translation only.

Face identifiers in MBML/BOM are enum member ids (XNeg, XPos, YNeg, YPos, ZNeg, ZPos) —
not integers and not authored as SCAD face strings. The SCAD literals "x-", "x+", … live on
Face as scad:value and are emit-only. Same pattern for Direction and Align.

How-to paths complement ReadFirst learning paths on ReadMe entry points:

ReadFirst (relation)     — mental learning order on ReadMe / README blocks
HowToIndex (relation)    — catalog of accomplishable how-tos on ReadMe
HowTo (branch)           — org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.* procedural blocks
HowToStep (relation)     — ordered steps inside a HowTo (document order = step order)
Prerequisite (relation)  — understand before starting a HowTo
Diagnostic (branch)      — org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* validator code documentation
Resolves (relation)      — Diagnostic → HowTo fix procedure

HowTo extends Documentation and lives in the documentation.howto subpackage — not
in core. Core holds root branches only. HowTo is not an executable workflow Task.

One mechanism: all navigation uses <references> and <see> with typed relation
attributes — no separate how-to aggregation on ReadMe. Automated process SPOE uses
Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap), separate from reading/how-to catalog on ReadMe.

Tooling (future):
• filter relation=ReadFirst → learn context bundle
• filter relation=HowToIndex → how-to menu
• load Diagnostic by code → follow Resolves → HowToStep chain

org.blockml.bml.README lists HowToIndex entries after ReadFirst entries. Future Bootstrap
subtypes (AgentBootstrap, CIBootstrap) supply automation SPOE members — not reading paths.

Implement with override="true" and a locally complete declaration (abstract defaults to false). To keep abstract, redeclare with abstract="true".
Emitted when a concrete Block still has an abstract member obligation from the inheritance/contract merge.

Implemented, validated, and mapping complete. Behavior is reliable and may be
depended on by downstream definitions and tooling. Implicit default when no status is declared
on an element — omit <status> and bml:status on Stable content.

In this context ${ … } forms are fixed tag recipes, not open Expression Language. Other roots, calls, or operators are invalid.
Emitted when a <bml:xml> body is not a literal local name, ${ bml:Self }, or ${ #this.name }.

Inheritance (baseType):
• Single inheritance — each Block has exactly one baseType (mandatory except org.blockml.bml.core.Block)
• Use for branch membership (ValueType, Language, domain base) and shared member fragments
• Framework branches inherit via org.blockml.bml.core.ValueType, Language, or domain bases
• Package org.blockml.bml.core — every root Block in this package must inherit directly from
  core:Block (Block itself omits baseType). Specializations of those branches live in sibling
  packages (type, relation, meta, documentation, …). Nested Sub-Blocks in core are exempt —
  they may extend any ancestor (for example Annotation.Directive and its descendants).
• final on Block or member prevents further override → BML_FINAL_BASE_TYPE / BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE

Contracts:
• Reusable partial Block definitions — not pure interfaces; may include default implementations
• Use when multiple Blocks share a member fragment without sharing a common baseType ancestor
• Declared on root block only via contracts aggregation — direct Block references
• Merge order: baseType chain → contracts (declaration order) → local declarations
• Contract may supply partial members (e.g. id type only); concrete Block completes defaults,
  constraints, and documentation
• subBlocks and compositions on contract types are ignored

Capabilities:
• All behaviour — init, get/set, render, parse, domain operations — express as Capabilities
• An implementation may be intent (PseudoCode / natural language), a companion template,
  or a host-evaluable function — no ranking (doc:CapabilitySemantics)
• Prefer PseudoCode or natural language when the body is intent for humans and LLMs
• Use Inbound/Outbound/Transformation/Action kinds to describe payload shape
• Public surface of a Block is Capabilities — Properties are internal configuration
• Declare throws for Exception types the Capability may raise
  (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[] — Java-style method throws; omit when none)

Constraints:
• Declare on Properties via constraints aggregation — Constraint Block instances
• Generic binding is automatic: Min/Max bind T from property type; MinItems/MaxItems from
  collection element type; MinLength/MaxLength from Text element type
• Use for validation rules expressible as reusable Constraint blocks (Min, Max, Pattern, …)
• Suggestions (optional Block instances of property type) guide editors — not validation

General: keep <is> stable; put cross-links in references; prefer explicit baseType over
implicit defaults; document partial members in contracts clearly.

Documentation formatting: block documentation is Markdown(English) by default — structure longer
prose with paragraphs, headings, lists, and inline code instead of one unbroken text; keep
summary plain text. Human-friendly formatting is a central part of BlockML
(doc:DocumentationModel).

Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for alternative Block type names in an aliases
aggregation on org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition only (root blocks and Sub-Blocks).
Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc names are Alias instances (for example
<meta:Alias value="Sub-Block" />). Comma-separated character content on <aliases> is
PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Alias instances — one value per trimmed token —
not to FixedAlias catalogue blocks. Not XML namespace prefix aliases. Not search tags —
use org.blockml.bml.meta.Keyword for those.

Domain libraries define catalogue alias blocks extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias.
Those types set value on the definition; references are empty fixed blocks (for example
<vocab:SubBlockAlias />). Type FQN is the catalogue identity; value, language, and
legacy resolve from the alias definition.

Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for search and discovery tags in a keywords aggregation
on org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc tags are
Keyword instances (for example <meta:Keyword value="inheritance" />). Comma-separated
character content on <keywords> is PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Keyword
instances — one value per trimmed token — not to FixedKeyword catalogue blocks.

Domain libraries define catalogue keyword blocks extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword
(for example org.example.keyword.Inheritance). Those types set value on the definition;
references are empty fixed blocks (for example <vocab:Inheritance />). Type FQN is the
catalogue identity; value, language, and weight resolve from the keyword definition.
Distinct from org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias (alternative Block type names on BlockDefinition).

Instantiable StructType with no fields. Unqualified name EmptyStruct resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.EmptyStruct.

The only compatible value is an empty object {}. EmptyStruct is a named, reusable unit
struct — the named counterpart of an anonymous empty StructType {}. It is not abstract:
use it wherever a StructType is required and no fields are needed, including Property
types, Capability inputType / outputType, and default generic bindings.

Language branch of BlockML. Declares an implementation language permitted on
Capability implementations (OpenSCAD, TypeScript, English, …). Natural languages for
documentation prose extend org.blockml.bml.language.NaturalLanguage; formal code and markup
languages extend ProgrammingLanguage and MarkupLanguage. ProgrammingLanguage and MarkupLanguage
declare optional generic L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language of
formal bodies — omit L unless the content language must be declared.

Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.
Align expression result type with the target member type.
Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.

LLMs repeatedly confuse member-declaration syntax with the syntax used when assigning members
on Block instances. The two most common mistakes are wrapping an instance Property in
<value> and wrapping instance Aggregation children in <composition>.

Incorrect on a Block instance:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition>…</composition></content></myns:MyBlock>

Two contexts, never mixed:

1. Definition context — a Property or Aggregation is being declared inside <properties>
   or <aggregations> (or an inherited member is filled on a Block definition).
2. Instance context — a concrete Block instance receives Property values or Aggregation
   children.

<value> is the value field of def:PropertyDefinition. <composition> is the
composition field of def:AggregationDefinition. Both are definition-context fields. They are
not general-purpose wrappers around instance payloads.

Critical authoring rule — inside a Block instance:
• NEVER introduce <value> as a wrapper around a Property assignment
• NEVER introduce <composition> as a wrapper around Aggregation children
Instead: the Property element (or Block attribute) contains the value; the Aggregation element
contains the child Blocks. Group instance children with bml:container, not composition.

PROPERTIES — definition. Inside <properties> the child element is a PropertyDefinition.
Its default value is the value field of that declaration. Element form is preferred when
serializing definitions:
<properties><description><value>BlockML core library</value></description></properties>
Compact attribute form on the declaration is also valid:
<properties><description value="BlockML core library"/></properties>
Do not specify both forms on the same declaration (conflicting payloads). Other declaration
fields (type, readOnly, override, constraints, suggestions) stay on this PropertyDefinition
element — they are not authored on domain instances.

PROPERTIES — Block instance. The instance is not a PropertyDefinition. It only supplies the
payload. Attribute form is preferred:
<myns:MyBlock myProperty="Hello!"/>
Element form is the Property element with direct character content — the element itself is
already the value container:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty>Hello!</myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — definition value field used as an instance wrapper:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Also incorrect as a wrapper (same category error):
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty value="Hello!"/></myns:MyBlock>
unless myProperty is actually named value (see exception below).

Exception — member whose name is value. PrimitiveEntity, TypeReferenceEntity, FilePathEntity
and similar types declare a Property named value. Then value="…" or <value>…</value>
on the Block instance is ordinary instance syntax for that member, not a PropertyDefinition
wrapper:
<type:FilePathEntity value="blockml-library.xsd"/>
Annotation value facets (e.g. <scad:value> under a property declaration) are a separate
namespace axis on PropertyDefinition.value — not instance wrappers. See doc:AnnotationModel.

AGGREGATIONS — definition. Inside <aggregations> the child element is an
AggregationDefinition. Its initial/default child structure is the composition field:
<aggregations><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></aggregations>
<composition> is allowed only as that definition field, nested inside the aggregation
member — never standalone (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION).

AGGREGATIONS — Block instance. Child Block instances are placed directly inside the
named Aggregation element. There is no composition wrapper and no default aggregation —
the aggregation must always be opened by member name:
<myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — composition wrapper on an instance:
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — implicit fill (bare child under the instance, aggregation not opened):
<myns:MyBlock><myns:Child/></myns:MyBlock>
The same rule applies recursively — a Block instance nested inside a definition composition
still fills its own aggregations without a composition wrapper:
<aggregations><myAggr><composition>
  <myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
</composition></myAggr></aggregations>
Outer <composition> is valid (myAggr is an Aggregation definition). Inner
<composition> under content is invalid (content is populated on a Block instance).

On instances, the virtual grouping element is bml:container — not composition. Both
composition (definitions) and bml:container (instances) host bml:if, bml:each, and bml:with.

Unified pattern:
Definition Property → value attribute or <value> wrapper on the PropertyDefinition
Definition Aggregation → <composition> wrapper on the AggregationDefinition
Instance Property → attribute on the Block, or direct Property element content
Instance Aggregation → named aggregation element containing child Block instances
(bml:container for grouping). Always open the aggregation; there is no default aggregation.
A PrimitiveEntity aggregation may also take comma-separated character content that expands to
instances with value set per token (core:PrimitiveEntity) — not a PropertyDefinition wrapper.

Capabilities on instances follow the Property pattern: attribute or child element, no extra
wrapper. readOnly effective members must not be authored on instances
(BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE). Declared exception types are the throws aggregation on the Capability
declaration — TypeReferenceEntity children (empty-QName sugar), not instance wrappers
(doc:CapabilitySemantics).
<value> and <composition> belong only to member declarations. On a Block instance
the Property element or attribute is already the value; the Aggregation element already holds
the child Blocks. Do not wrap instance payloads in those definition fields.

MachineBlocks domain base Block. Carries presets aggregation and basePresets
association for domain-specific preset resolution. Preset merge is compiler logic; Customizer
output is render-target logic.

MachineBlocks domain types under com.machineblocks.bml.core:

Block — abstract domain base (baseType Entity). Carries name, presets aggregation, and
basePresets association.
ConfigProfile — abstract parameter surface (baseType Block). Defines the native properties whose
conventional home is the config profile: calibration, printer profile, and clearances that
follow the printer. Not a resolver constraint — settings may still override any parameter.
Content blocks do not extend ConfigProfile.
CompositeBlock — Block with default _parts aggregation for child block instances.
NativeBlock — final leaf geometry Block. Maps 1:1 to the native geometry primitive at render
  time. baseType is ConfigProfile. Together with ConfigProfile, the SSOT for all native MachineBlocks
  parameters: config-conventional properties are defined on ConfigProfile, brick and feature
  properties on NativeBlock. Uses children for nested native geometry
  instead of _parts. Must not be used as baseType for custom Block definitions.
Set — CompositeBlock for LEGO-style builds: palette via presets, placed instances in _parts,
  assembly order in _steps.
Step — final assembly instruction Block. baseType is org.blockml.bml.core.Block (framework
  Block), not mbcore:Block / Entity — a sibling outside the Entity → mbcore:Block tree.
  part association references a placed _parts instance by bml:id; document order in _steps is
  build order.

Hierarchy: Entity → mbcore:Block → ConfigProfile → NativeBlock. CompositeBlock → Set stays under
mbcore:Block. NativeBlock is final. Step sits on org.blockml.bml.core.Block → Step.

Class identity is the Block FQN. Instance identity inside composition uses bml:id (nested paths
use ::). There is no separate Placement type — direction, offset, and related placement data
live on the placed instances.

MachineBlocks domain ValueTypes live in com.machineblocks.bml.type.*. They are the SSOT for
type shapes used by NativeBlock properties and other domain members. Do not redefine types from
Markdown or YAML.

Categories (illustrative — see package members for the full inventory):

Atomic enums — Axis, Face, Direction, Align, StudType, HoleType, Gender, and related.
Axis containers — AxisXY(T), AxisXYZ(T), AxisAB(T) for per-axis values.
Face / side maps — FaceMapXY, FaceMapXYZ, CornerMap, Per-side and hole-edge maps.
Size and offset — SizeXYZ, SizeXY, SizeAB, OffsetXYZ, OffsetXY, OffsetAB, RotationXYZ.
Domain compounds — Connector, ScrewHole, WallGap / RecessWallGap, Port, Grille, SelectiveGrid,
  rounding maps, quality profiles, PCB types.

Naming uses XYZ / XY / AB axis keys — not 3D / 2D labels.

MBOM values are canonical. Render targets serialize those values (for SCAD mappings see the
SCAD TypesAndSerialization documentation). NativeBlock property type attributes reference these
types directly.

MachineBlocks follows a layered architecture:

MBML / BML (authoring)
  ↓ parse (@blockml/parser)
Urmodell — Canonical BOM (immutable; MBOM is the MachineBlocks specialization)
  ↓ Stage 2 — Validator (pragmatic fork; resolve only)
  ↓ Stage 3 — Render Target (reference: OpenSCAD)
STL / 3MF (or other target artifacts)

MBML is the declarative authoring format for blocks, sets, and related MachineBlocks
documents. Authors describe typed, parameterized elements without knowledge of any
render target. XML is the sole BML serialization for V1 and V2.

MBOM is the renderer-independent domain model layered on BOM Core — not a second SSOT.
The BOM Compiler parses BML into an immutable Urmodell (Canonical BOM); MBOM extends that
graph with MachineBlocks types, ConfigProfile and NativeBlock parameters, and SCAD conventions.
Validation operates on the lossless BOM (Stage 2 pragmatic fork). Composition expansion,
expression evaluation, and target emit are Stage 3 — the renderer chooses Urmodell,
the default pragmatic model, or its own forks.

A render target serializes that model into a concrete output language. The MachineBlocks V3
SCAD library is the reference render target: OpenSCAD files that OpenSCAD turns into STL or
3MF. MBOM/BOM is canonical; SCAD is a serialization — not the other way around.

Core principle: one native geometry primitive (NativeBlock → mb_block()) with a large
parameter space (SSOT: ConfigProfile.bml and NativeBlock.bml). Complexity comes from parameter combinations,
composition of multiple blocks, and nesting — not from many unrelated primitives.

MachineBlocks is a parametric system for generating LEGO-compatible 3D blocks. Primary use is
3D printing (STL / 3MF); the same geometry model also supports general 3D modeling workflows.

The system is a foundation for modular, printable machines: bricks, panels, enclosures, and
functional assemblies built from typed, parameterized blocks.

MachineBlocks is a domain on top of BlockML. Authoring uses MBML (MachineBlocks Markup
Language). The canonical representation is MBOM (MachineBlocks Object Model). Render targets —
OpenSCAD is the reference — serialize MBOM into target-specific output. Direct OpenSCAD Block
Files remain supported as an advanced and legacy authoring path.

MachineBlocks sizes the world in a unit stack:

mm → mbu → grid → block geometry

unitMbuToMm (default 1.6) is the millimetre length of one mbu (MachineBlocks Unit).
unitGridToMbu is SizeXYZ (default {x: 5, y: 5, z: 2}): mbu per grid step on each axis for a
1×1 plate. At defaults that is 8×8×3.2 mm. A size of [1, 1, 1] is therefore a plate — not a
cube. The default XY-to-Z grid ratio is 2.5:1; cube-like blocks need Z ≈ 2.5× the XY grid
extent (for example [2, 2, 5] → 16×16×16 mm). X and Y may differ (unitGridToMbu is full XYZ).

Absolute size along an axis is
size[axis] × unitGridToMbu[axis] × unitMbuToMm × scale.

The bounding box is defined exclusively by size. Other parameters change visible geometry
inside that box; they do not redefine the spatial contract.

Geometry parameters use mbu or grid units. Calibration adjustments (for example baseAdjustment)
use absolute millimetres and must not scale with the global scale factor.

MarkupLanguage for BlockML (BML) document implementations on Capabilities — block
definitions, library catalogs, and other structured BML markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language inside the BML body — bare BML
is BML(English).

MarkupLanguage for JSON document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare JSON is JSON(English).

MarkupLanguage for Markdown prose — documentation bodies and Markdown document
implementations on Capabilities — with lightweight structure (headings, lists, links, code
fences).

Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) is forwarded from MarkupLanguage and names
the content language of the Markdown body: Markdown = Markdown(English), Markdown(German) for
German prose. Because L is forwarded rather than bound, Markdown(NaturalLanguage) is a usable
type bound — def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language binds
Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage, where the bare-language alternative is shorthand for
Markdown in that language.

Also the default content language of documentation prose: Markdown(English) is the default value
of language on def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation, so every <documentation> body is
Markdown unless it declares otherwise. summary is plain text and never Markdown. CDATA is an XML
serialization detail — Markdown itself never requires it. See doc:DocumentationModel —
Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA.

MarkupLanguage for XML document implementations on Capabilities — templates,
configuration, or structured markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English)
for the content/text language inside the markup — bare XML is XML(English).

MarkupLanguage for YAML document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare YML is YML(English).

Maturity is expressed with Status Block references — not free strings or boolean flags.

Core status blocks (package org.blockml.bml.status.*):
Stable — implemented, tested, and mapping complete; reliable behaviour (implicit default).
Draft — definition exists; implementation or mapping incomplete, untested, or
  intentionally divergent; may change.
Stub — placeholder; shape declared, behaviour not yet specified; validates OK;
  renderer may stub/log or abort.
Deprecated — retained for compatibility; do not use in new work.

Default is Stable. Status inherits downward; authors declare status only when diverging from
the inherited effective status.

At <status> and bml:status reference sites, unqualified names resolve to
org.blockml.bml.status.* — bare names are correct there
(e.g. <status>Draft</status>, bml:status="Deprecated").
Explicit prefixes or FQNs remain valid everywhere (status:Draft ≡ Draft at those sites).
Bare status names are invalid outside specialized status reference sites.

SCAD implementation status and MBOM mapping status may differ independently for the same
parameter or type. Use Draft with an explicit note when they are misaligned.

mb_block() is the single public native geometry module of the MachineBlocks V3 SCAD library.
All printable leaf geometry goes through it — complexity is parameters, composition, and nesting.

Public signature:
mb_block(config = undef, settings = undef)

config and settings are optional arrays of [key, value] pairs (pseudo-maps). Resolution order
for each parameter: settings → config → default. Never read the arrays by hand inside Block
Modules. mb_params_merge, mb_params_get, and mb_params_filter do not apply that resolution;
their contracts, together with the composite preview helpers, are in HelperApi.

Parameter access rule (mandatory inside every Block Module):

• Native — every property declared on com.machineblocks.bml.core.NativeBlock is a native
  parameter. In SCAD it MUST be read via its dedicated getter:
  mb_param_[propertyName](config, settings)
  optional third argument: block-specific default override.
  Example: size → mb_param_size(config, settings)

• Custom — any other parameter (module-specific, not a NativeBlock property) MUST be read via
  the generic getter:
  mb_param(config, settings, "name", default)
  Example: brick1SizeY → mb_param(config, settings, "brick1SizeY", 2)

Never invent mb_param_* for custom names. Never use mb_param() for NativeBlock properties.
Never access config/settings arrays directly.

Reference: com.machineblocks.bml.examples.Cross (Cross.scad) shows both sides in one module —
native getters for size, studs, baseColor, … and mb_param() for brick1SizeY, brick2SizeX,
brick1OffsetY, brick2OffsetX.

config carries environment, calibration, and shared profile values. settings carry instance
overrides for one call. Calibration adjustments belong in config profiles — not as routine
settings on content blocks.

Parameter inventory, types, defaults, and documentation are defined on ConfigProfile and NativeBlock —
together they are the SSOT. ConfigProfile holds the config-conventional properties; NativeBlock holds
brick and feature properties and inherits ConfigProfile. SCAD docs explain the call model; they do
not redefine the parameter set.

MBML (MachineBlocks Markup Language) is the declarative authoring format for MachineBlocks.
It is BML specialized for the MachineBlocks domain: blocks, sets, presets, and composition
described as typed XML without OpenSCAD knowledge. XML is the sole BML serialization for
V1 and V2.

The BOM Compiler parses BML into an immutable Urmodell (Canonical BOM). MBOM is the
MachineBlocks domain specialization of that model — types, ConfigProfile and NativeBlock parameters, and
domain block kinds — not a separate compiler product. Render targets interpret the BOM/MBOM
graph (Urmodell, pragmatic fork, or their own forks); they do not redefine the domain model.

Authoring flow: write .bml sources → parse to Urmodell → validate (Stage 2) → render with a
registered target (reference: machineblocks-v3-scad). Direct .scad Block Files bypass
MBML/MBOM and remain an advanced path; prefer MBML for new domain content.

MBML authoring mirrors the shared pattern inventory (DecisionFramework / ModulePatterns):

1. Primitive Wrapper / Native leaf — lowers to NativeBlock parameters, including those inherited
from ConfigProfile. One body, one spatial contract. Custom brick types typically extend CompositeBlock
or Block and lower to NativeBlock instances — NativeBlock itself is final and cannot be a
baseType. Do not extend ConfigProfile; it is only the parameter surface NativeBlock inherits.

2. Simple semantic Block — named domain type with defaults and a focused parameter surface;
still one native geometry realization at the leaf.

3. Composite Block — _parts (or nested children) for L/T/cross shapes, enclosures, channels,
and multi-body devices. Parent size is the outer bbox; parts carry direction and offset.
Set is a Composite specialization: palette in presets, placed instances in _parts, optional
ordered _steps for assembly instructions.

4. Helper / Form — shared geometry helpers, not content products. Primarily a SCAD Block File
concern (see ModulePatterns / ScadDecisionRules); rarely published as an MBML product Block.

Decision rule: if a single native call cannot express the topology without breaking the
capability boundary, author a Composite Block. Prefer composition over baseCrop and over mixing
incompatible shape modifiers in one leaf.

Member and Sub-Block visibility controls BlockML access only — which definitions may reference,
read, or set a member or Sub-Block. It does not prescribe how a renderer manifests visibility.
Renderers always see the entire Canonical BOM (public, protected, and private). Visibility
restricts authoring access, not technical BOM access.

Naming convention (primary signal):
• myVar — public
• _myVar — protected
• __myVar — private

The prefix is BlockML visibility, not logical member identity. Collision checking uses the
normalizedLogicalName with visibility prefixes stripped (myVar / _myVar / __myVar → myVar).
Members that differ only by visibility prefix must not coexist in the same Block →
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT. A logical member exists exactly once with exactly one
visibility.

Override matching uses normalizedLogicalName. A child may redeclare with a different visibility
prefix only when the change widens access:
• protected → public — allowed
• private → any — forbidden (BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE)
• public → protected/private, or protected → private — forbidden (BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING)
Effective visibility and authored name come from the child declaration. Member-level bml:xml may
change on the same override.

Formal access (D = declaring Block, C = Block whose definition contains the access, I = instance
type, O = immediate composition owner of that instance):
• public — always
• private — only when C = D (owning composite does not gain access to private members of
  contained Sub-Block instances)
• protected — when C = D, or C inherits from D, or C = O, or C inherits from I.
  Only the immediate composition owner grants protected configuration access on children — not
  the entire outer composition hierarchy.

Aggregation members: visibility also controls which bml:id values may be referenced
(basePresets, Step.part, {BlockFQN}::{id}, …):
• public — cross-document {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id}; unqualified ids within permitted access
• protected — declaring Block and its child Blocks (derived / Sub-Blocks in the same tree)
• private — declaring Block definition only
No separate export flag on composition or bml:container — reachability follows the aggregation
member's visibility. Qualified cross-document references require a public target aggregation and
a literal static bml:id.

Optional visibility property on members (and optional root-level visibility on Sub-Blocks) must
match the naming convention → mismatch BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH. Root Blocks must not declare
root-level visibility.

Validator diagnostics (access checks do not alter the Canonical BOM):
BML_PRIVATE_MEMBER_ACCESS, BML_PROTECTED_MEMBER_ACCESS,
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT, BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH, BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING,
BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE (private cannot be overridden).

Declared on org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition as visibility (and related override
rules). Sub-Block visibility uses the same naming convention — see also Sub-Block authoring
rules on org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition.

Member-shaped directive under an annotation namespace. name is fixed to "*"
— the concrete local name comes from the authoring QName (e.g. scad:value). Specialized by

Meta-model type for document-root block documents. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition, overrides definition (default RootBlockDefinition),
and adds the embeddedBlocks aggregation (Inline Library — virtual .bml files co-located in one
BomDocument). subBlocks is inherited from BlockDefinition.

The definition property defaults to org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition when
<definition> is omitted on the document root. Embedded entries use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition (see EmbeddedBlockDefinition) — they are not
RootBlockDefinition instances. Sub-Blocks use SubBlockDefinition — sibling specialization.

embeddedBlocks is allowed only on the document root. Each child is an EmbeddedBlockDefinition
(virtual file): own FQN from mandatory <type>, own members and subBlocks, no nested
embeddedBlocks. Nested embeds are forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Within this document,
embedded FQNs shadow library/file definitions; duplicate embed FQNs →
BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK; externally embeds remain invisible.

Meta-model type for embedded Block documents — virtual .bml files inlined under
the document root's <embeddedBlocks> aggregation. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition (subBlocks, identity, members) and overrides
definition to default EmbeddedBlockDefinition.

Embedded blocks are full Block documents. Authoring is the same as the document root
(doc:DocumentFormat): preferred type tag (<acme:MyBlock>), legacy <block> plus
<type>. The resolved type is the FQN (not nested under the root) and must be fully
qualified. They may declare subBlocks and generics like any Block. They must
not declare <embeddedBlocks> — nesting is forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Only the
document root (RootBlockDefinition) may own embeddedBlocks; compose fat artifacts by listing
virtual files flat at the root (bundlers flatten nested packages when merging).

Within the BomDocument, each embedded FQN shadows the corresponding library or file-based
BlockDefinition. Duplicate FQNs among embeds → BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK. Externally,
embeds are invisible.

Meta-model type for nested Sub-Block documents within a BomDocument. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition and overrides definition (default SubBlockDefinition).
Shared identity, members, and subBlocks are inherited from BlockDefinition — Sub-Block-specific
identity rules live here.

Block identity conventions for Sub-Blocks (see 02_mbml.md — Type References and Block Identity):
• Sub-Block: semantically nested type within the same BomDocument as the root block — does not
  open its own document or library scope. Analogous to a Java static nested class: may declare
  own <genericTypes>; does not see enclosing Block generics (forward with applications).
  Uses org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition
  as definition meta-model — default org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition when
  <definition> is omitted. name is the local identity (required) — preferred authoring:
  the element local name under <subBlocks> is the Sub-Block name (<MyBlock>);
  child <name> is then optional (doc:DocumentFormat). type is normally
  omitted and derived recursively from the immediate enclosing block as
  resolve(parent.type) + "." + name (BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH when an explicit type does not
  match). Sub-Blocks may declare further Sub-Blocks to any depth (for example
  com.foo.Vehicle.Engine.Cylinder). Unqualified nested names resolve enclosing-chain first
  (02_mbml.md — Unqualified nested type resolution). Sub-Blocks must not declare embeddedBlocks
  (BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK).

Root blocks use org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition; embedded virtual files use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition — sibling specializations of
BlockDefinition.

OpenSCAD is the reference MachineBlocks render target. It is not the canonical representation
of blocks — MBOM is. The SCAD target serializes MBOM into MachineBlocks V3 .scad files that
OpenSCAD renders to STL or 3MF.

The target registers as machineblocks-v3-scad. V1 handles two base domain kinds:
Block (and descendants that lower to block modules) via a block processor, and Set via a set
processor (STEPS and view submodules).

MachineBlocks World convention: leaf NativeBlock ↔ mb_block(); composition becomes a nested
mb_block() tree; domain types lower to mb_block() settings. Other BlockML render targets may
emit entirely different shapes — this mapping is MachineBlocks-specific.

For 1:1 Block→file emit, Manifestation packages replace definition segment bml with scad
(com.machineblocks.bml.X → com.machineblocks.scad.X for path and mb__ module names). See
BlockFileStructure. Other targets may choose a different segment; this is not a platform rule.

Direct authoring of V3 Block Files (hand-written or AI-generated) remains supported and bypasses
MBML/MBOM. As MBML matures, that path becomes advanced/legacy for domain content.

Optional visibility on members and Sub-Blocks must agree with public / _protected / __private naming. When omitted, visibility is derived from the name.
Emitted when an explicit visibility property does not match the naming-convention prefix on the name.

Override matching uses normalizedLogicalName. Widening (protected → public) is allowed; narrowing is forbidden. Private members cannot be overridden at all.
Emitted when an override reduces visibility (e.g. public → protected, or protected → private).

Validation Stages 1–3 (Parser / Validator / Renderer) — glossary in 06_compiler.md.
Semantic validation is the validator and the LSP. XSD is not a standard check; the XSD
compiler remains available but is not used by default (doc:DocumentFormat).
Self-hosting: CLI bootstraps TypeRegistry from framework BML before user projects.

In this compiler pipeline a Capability body is often a companion template the renderer
emits, or a name the renderer maps to a target construct. That is one interpretation
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). Hosts — including a future validator that evaluates
PrimitiveType.parseValue — may execute a deterministic implementation body. The model
does not forbid executable Capability implementations.

Plate-grid unit along X and Y. A 1×1 plate footprint is one GridUnitXY in each
horizontal axis. Size in mbu via unitGridToMbu.x / unitGridToMbu.y (default 5 mbu per
GridUnitXY). Distinct from GridUnitZ — vertical plate height uses a different mbu scale.

Plate-grid unit along Z (stack height). One plate layer is one GridUnitZ.
Size in mbu via unitGridToMbu.z (default 2 mbu per GridUnitZ). Distinct from GridUnitXY —
horizontal footprint uses a different mbu scale.

PrimitiveType declares parseValue — a Transformation from authored Text to bml:Self that
throws exception:InvalidValueException. Concrete primitives implement a deterministic
TypeScript body (host-evaluable reading of doc:CapabilitySemantics). The BML outputType is
always bml:Self — the TypeScript return (number, string, boolean) is FunctionMapping / host
encoding, not the Capability signature.

parseValue is lexical only:
• Input is XML attribute or element text, already tokenized by the parser as Text
• Success means the text is a value of this PrimitiveType
• Failure throws InvalidValueException; a validating host reports diag:BML_INVALID_VALUE
• The body sees the type definition, not the Property's configured type instance — no
  this.min / this.max

After a successful parse, in this order:
1. Type instance configuration — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}, Text{maxLength: 50}
   (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration)
2. Property constraints — Pattern, Min, Max, … (doc:ConstraintsModel)
3. Existence checks on Reference types — TypeReference, InstanceReference, PropertyReference /
   … (doc:TypeSystemOverview). parseValue does not consult the TypeRegistry.

Inheritance: Text implements identity (every string is Text). Number implements a numeric
literal; Integer, Decimal, and Float refine. Temporal leaves parseValue abstract; Date, Time,
and DateTime implement ISO forms. Identifier types implement syntax; Reference subtypes inherit
that syntax and add existence in the validator. PackageSelector / TypeSelector accept wildcard
patterns of which Identifier is the concrete form. URI requires an RFC 3986 scheme; URL is an
absolute http/https web address; FilePath is a non-empty path without NUL or line breaks
(existence on disk is not part of parseValue).

parseValue does not cover multiplicity or unions (TypeExpression on the reference, element-wise),
StructType field walks, EnumType membership, or Constant(T){value} equality. Those stay
validator-side.

Bootstrap: the compiler still tokenizes framework BML as text. parseValue runs on loaded
property values after TypeRegistry bootstrap. Hard-coded bootstrap parsers for Text, Integer,
Boolean, and TypeIdentifier remain until a host evaluates these bodies.

Private members (__name) are usable only within the declaring Block's definition — including instances of the declaring type in that same definition. Composition ownership does not lift private encapsulation of contained Sub-Block instances.
Emitted when a private member is read or set outside the Block definition that declares it.

Procedure for a new domain Block type:
1. Choose baseType from the framework or domain branch.
2. Author the document root as the type tag (doc:DocumentFormat). Nested Sub-Blocks use
   the unqualified name as the element tag; embeds use the same tag-as-type form as the
   root. Legacy <block> wrappers remain valid. Declare documentation metadata
   (is, documentation, optional summary).
3. Add properties, aggregations, associations, or capabilities.
4. Add constraints, capabilities, and examples as needed.
5. Place the file under the nearest Library.bml when the type belongs to a library
   (membership is directory location, not a catalog list). Version is optional.
Create a root .bml file whose root tag is the type, with is, documentation,
baseType, and member containers as needed. Place the file under the owning Library.bml
when it belongs to a library; version may be omitted (inherited from that Library).

Procedure for adding a constraint:
1. Confirm the definition element extends ConstrainableDefinition (Block or member).
2. Add a constraints container if absent.
3. Insert a Constraint Block reference (element name = FQN via xmlns prefix).
4. Optionally attach a validation reference on the constraint instance for rule enforcement.
5. Run the validator — BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH when branch compatibility fails.
Declare a constraints container on a ConstrainableDefinition element and add a Constraint
reference as a direct child. The embedding context binds the constraint target automatically —
no target property in BML.

Procedure when an expression-related BML_EXPR_* (or embed) diagnostic is reported:
1. Confirm host context — whole-value member ${ } vs interpolated Text holes vs implementation
   <$ $> (doc:Expressions, doc:EmbeddedExpressions).
2. Interpolation holes — Restricted Profile only (property access, literals, +, #strings.*,
   #math.*). Not desugared to concatenation. @model / @bean / Capability calls / each-with
   variables → BML_EXPR_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_INTERPOLATION. Unclosed ${ → BML_EXPR_SYNTAX_ERROR.
   Interpolation on a non-Text member → BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH. this without # is a member
   (#this.this), not the instance.
3. Syntax errors — check delimiters, quotes, operators; embeds must not nest <$ $>.
4. Unknown property — verify member exists in scope; StructType fields by name only (not [0]).
5. Unknown bean / builtin — declare bml:bean Aggregation or use a V1 #built-in.
6. Type / payload mismatch — align expression result with member type; map call args via
   FunctionMapping (doc:FunctionMappingModel).
7. Linking (@bean.capa without parens) — source Outbound, target Inbound, compatible payloads.
8. Relative @model: — ensure a parent Aggregation established binding context.
9. V1 — avoid deferred @bean execution / model / linking features until implemented.
Resolve ${ }, interpolated Text, and <$ $> expression diagnostics — syntax,
unknown refs, type/payload mismatches, Restricted Profile, linking, and model context.

Procedure when composition placement fails validation:
1. On Block definitions — nest <composition> inside an aggregation member element; never
   leave it standalone (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION).
2. On Block instances — always open aggregations by member name; no composition wrapper
   and no default aggregation. Bare child Block instances directly under the parent
   instance are invalid. Same rule as Properties: do not wrap instance values in
   <value> (doc:MemberAuthoring).
3. Inherited aggregation fill — use override="true"; omit unchanged type.
4. Shared sibling values — bml:with on composition or bml:container (see doc:BmlDirectives).
5. Instance ID reachability — follows aggregation member visibility (doc:MemberVisibility).
Resolve standalone composition errors and clarify definition vs instance aggregation
fill, including bml:container and bml:with usage.

Procedure when the validator reports a visibility-related BML_* code:
1. Identify whether the site is a member or a Sub-Block (same naming convention).
2. Confirm the intended visibility via name prefix: public / _protected / __private.
3. For access errors — move the use into an allowed context (declaring Block, inheritance,
   immediate composition owner for protected) or widen the declaration if appropriate.
4. For override narrowing — keep or widen visibility; never narrow; private cannot be overridden.
5. For duplicate variants — keep exactly one normalizedLogicalName with one visibility.
6. For root-level <visibility> on a root Block — remove it (Sub-Blocks only).
Resolve private/protected member or Sub-Block access errors, visibility mismatches,
narrowing on override, and duplicate visibility-prefix variants.

Procedure when the validator reports an override/merge-related BML_* code:
1. Determine whether the local member is new or merges with baseType/contracts identity
   (resolvedNamespace + normalizedLogicalName).
2. Merging redeclaration → set override="true" on every layer (including contract completion).
3. New member → do not set override="true".
4. Abstract obligation on a concrete Block → complete locally (type/value/implementation) with
   override="true", or keep abstract="true" on the redeclaration.
5. final or private parent → do not override; change modeling approach.
6. readOnly → set values on definitions/overrides only, not on Block instances.
7. Aggregation fill-only override → omit unchanged type (BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE).
Resolve override-required / without-parent, abstract-not-implemented, final override,
readOnly instance writes, and redundant aggregation type warnings.

Procedure when the validator reports BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE:
1. Locate the field whose declared type is TypeReference or TypeReferenceEntity (or a
   subtype). The XML name of the field does not matter. Fields typed TypeIdentifier
   (and not TypeReference) do not emit this diagnostic.
2. Confirm the expanded FQN matches a registered BlockDefinition — or treat the finding as
   a missing dependency (library not loaded), not as proof the document is ill-formed.
3. Check xmlns prefix maps to the intended namespace on this document.
4. Confirm the defining file sits under the owning Library.bml when loaded via a library
   (membership is location, not a catalog list).
5. Verify dependency libraries and bootstrap order load the defining catalogue first.
Verify FQN spelling, xmlns prefix resolution, that the defining file sits under an
owning Library.bml (or is loaded as standalone), and bootstrap load order so the
referenced type is registered in TypeRegistry before validation.

Procedure when type identity or reference resolution fails:
1. Classify the Block role — root, Sub-Block, or embedded virtual file.
2. Root — require type from the element tag (preferred) or child <type> (legacy
   <block>); optional name must equal lastSegment(resolve(type)).
3. Sub-Block — require name from the element tag (preferred <MyBlock>) or child
   <name> (legacy <block>); omit type or match parentType + "." + name from the
   immediate enclosing block; never declare embeddedBlocks.
4. Embedded — same authoring as the root: type from the element tag or child <type>;
   type must be fully qualified; FQN is not nested under the root; no nested embeds.
5. Unqualified names — use nested resolution (innermost first) or context-bound implicit
   namespace; grandchildren need a relative path; otherwise qualify with xmlns/FQN.
6. Ambiguous short Sub-Block names that match the root — rename or use qualified references.
Resolve root/Sub-Block/embedded identity mismatches, ambiguous or unqualified references,
and definition-role errors.

Property-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective PropertyDefinition.
When validation is set, the validator requires readOnly=true on the Property (authored or
derived). Reference implementation for PropertyConstraint branch.

Property-shaped member directive (name="*") under scad. Authoring QNames such
as <properties><scad:value/></properties> are property members in this
annotation namespace — catalog metadata for SCAD render (e.g. MBEnum), not Definition
meta-model types and not nested value facets.

Protected members (_name) allow access when C=D, C inherits from D, C is the immediate composition owner O, or C inherits from instance type I. Outer composition ancestors do not receive protected configuration access.
Emitted when a protected member is used outside declaring Block, inheritance, or immediate composition-owner context.

Protected Sub-Blocks (_Name) are visible inside the enclosing Block definition and derived Blocks — not from arbitrary external documents.
Emitted when a protected Sub-Block is referenced outside the enclosing definition and its derived Blocks.

PseudoCode (org.blockml.bml.language.PseudoCode) is a ProgrammingLanguage for free-form
pseudocode Capability implementations. The code must be internally consistent but is
otherwise unconstrained — an LLM may interpret it. Content/text language follows
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) — declare L only when the prose
is not English.

Why PseudoCode exists:
• Capability implementations need a stable intent form that humans and LLMs can read
• PseudoCode avoids premature binding to Java, TypeScript, SCAD, or Python syntax
• Intent descriptions in PseudoCode stay stable across Worlds and hosts

When to use PseudoCode:
• Documenting intended behaviour on Capabilities during design (intent reading)
• Framework and domain blocks where the semantic contract matters more than a host body
• Blocks read by LLMs for code generation — PseudoCode is the preferred intent layer

When to use concrete languages:
• org.blockml.bml.language.TypeScript, OpenSCAD, Python, … as a companion template a
  renderer transpiles or emits, or as a host-evaluable function a toolchain runs
• Block definitions may restrict permitted languages via the languages aggregation

PseudoCode is the preferred intent dialect — not the only allowed implementation form.
A Capability may also carry a companion template or a deterministic host-evaluable body
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). A compiler renderer mapping names to target constructs remains
one valid interpretation, not a model restriction.

Publishable BlockML core library (org.blockml.bml.Library). Provides the framework grammar:
core branches (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Language, Status, Relation, Constraint, Validation, Capability, Exception, Definition, Group),
group branch (org.blockml.bml.group.MemberGroup, org.blockml.bml.group.BlockGroup),
concrete value types and constraints, implementation languages, built-in services, lifecycle
status blocks, the Definition meta-model branch (org.blockml.bml.definition.*), the language
annotation (org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation), bootstrap
documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*), how-to blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.*),
diagnostic blocks (org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.*), and definition metadata
(org.blockml.bml.meta.Keyword, org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias, org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword,
org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias). Keyword and Alias are PrimitiveEntity(Text) — ad-hoc
instances and comma-separated value sugar. Fixed* freeze value and companion members as
readOnly; domain libraries extend them for catalogue-controlled tags and alternative names.

Root Blocks in org.blockml.bml.core must inherit directly from core:Block; nested Sub-Blocks
in that package are exempt (doc:ModelingGuidelines).

Membership is location: a Block belongs to this library when this Library.bml is the nearest
library walking up from the block file (search stops one level below srcDir). Nested
Library.bml files own their subtree. This descriptor is not a member of itself. Version 3.0.0
is inherited by members that omit their own <version> (framework convention: version often
only on Library.bml).

Publishable MachineBlocks root library (com.machineblocks.bml.Library). Groups shared domain
ValueTypes, Units, MemberGroups (com.machineblocks.bml.group.*), ScadAnnotation, curated
documentation blocks under com.machineblocks.bml.documentation.{concept,mbml,scad}, brick
types (com.machineblocks.bml.bricks.*), calibration, and examples. Membership is the nearest
Library.bml by directory, not a catalog list.

README block for the BlockML core library. Start with references marked relation=ReadFirst —
thirty-seven documentation blocks in mental learning order. The early entries form the BlockML
conceptual core — the core use cases, the type system, and the expression language
(${ } and <$ $>).
Later entries cover conventions, authoring rules (visibility, overrides, member authoring,
composition, annotations, directives, type identity, Sub-Blocks, contracts, constraints),
organisation, and background knowledge.

Library.bml points here via the required readMe aggregation (<blockml:README />).
Tooling filters references where relation=ReadFirst to build a curated learning context bundle;
relation=HowToIndex lists accomplishable procedural how-tos for humans, agents, and CI. Automated
process SPOE uses Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap) — not this ReadMe.

README block for the MachineBlocks root library (com.machineblocks.bml.Library).
Start with references marked relation=ReadFirst — curated documentation in mental learning
order across concept (renderer-agnostic), mbml (authoring), and scad (OpenSCAD render target).
Library.bml points here via the required readMe aggregation (<mb:README />).

Recommended package form for BML definitions — Blocks, Libraries, Types, Languages, Services,
Capabilities, and all other BlockML definitions:

• <domain>.bml.*

Examples:
• org.blockml.bml.*
• com.machineblocks.bml.*
• com.example.bml.*

A bml segment in the FQN package is a recommendation, not a requirement. It keeps Block types
conflict-free with companion packages that occupy the domain without a language marker — for
example a Java package com.example.Foo beside a Block com.example.bml.Foo. FQNs outside
<domain>.bml.* are valid; BML_OUTSIDE_BML_NAMESPACE is obsolete and is not emitted.
Physical source layout mirrors the FQN: blocks/org/blockml/bml/core/Block.bml defines
org.blockml.bml.core.Block.

Typical BlockML branches (all under org.blockml.bml.*):
• org.blockml.bml.core.* — framework base types (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Status, Capability, Exception, Library, …)
• org.blockml.bml.annotation.* — concrete Annotations (BmlAnnotation)
• org.blockml.bml.type.* — bootstrap ValueTypes
• org.blockml.bml.service.* — built-in expression services (#math, #strings, …)
• org.blockml.bml.language.* — implementation language types
• org.blockml.bml.capability.* — Capability type branches
• org.blockml.bml.definition.* — Definition meta-model (orthogonal to Annotations)
• org.blockml.bml.documentation.* — bootstrap documentation blocks
• org.blockml.bml.status.* / constraint.* / validation.* / relation.* / unit.* — matching branches

xmlns prefixes are BML-semantic only when they target a Package or an Annotation:
• Package — type addressing (xmlns:core="org.blockml.bml.core")
• Annotation — directives (xmlns:bml="org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation")
Other URI bindings (schemaLocation keys) are not BML-semantic type namespaces.
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is not a standard
feature (doc:DocumentFormat). Undeclared
prefix → BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX; non-Package/Annotation target →
BML_INVALID_NAMESPACE_TARGET; colliding prefixes across a bundle →
BML_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_COLLISION.

XML prefix convention (required authoring practice — BOM stores FQNs; compiler does not
rewrite aliases). Rule of thumb: a bare short prefix always means BlockML. Domain mirrors of
the same segment use a domain token in front (MachineBlocks → mb):
• core → org.blockml.bml.core · type → org.blockml.bml.type · unit → org.blockml.bml.unit
• lang → org.blockml.bml.language · status / def / constraint / validation / … → matching
  org.blockml.bml.*
• mbcore → com.machineblocks.bml.core · mbt → …type · mbunit → …unit
• bricks / cal / scad — collective or annotation packages (descriptive OK when no collision)
Do not steal framework aliases (xmlns:core="com.machineblocks.bml.core" is wrong). Do not use
legacy bcore / btype. Other domains use their own short token (ac → acore / atype / aunit).

Member and facet QNames: optional XML prefix on member element names supplies the member
namespace (resolved via xmlns; unprefixed → default empty namespace). Prefixed member QNames
that are Annotation Member directives (name="*") resolve to that Annotation — see
doc:AnnotationModel. There is no namespace= attribute on members.

Domain libraries typically follow the same recommended <domain>.bml.* layout
(com.machineblocks.bml.core / bricks / type / annotation.*, …).

npm workspace packages (@blockml/core, @blockml/parser, …) are deployment units — not
identical to FQN namespaces. TypeScript toolchain code ships in package src/ directories;
it is not a BML definition and does not receive a BML FQN.

Records a documentation link from the current definition to another Block type,
package, Block instance, definition element, repository markdown file, or external URL. References
connect types to types or types to instances for documentation purposes — they are not
instance-to-instance model links (those are Associations / AssociationDefinition). Rendered
as a see element inside the references container on any
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition (alongside changelog and examples). Maps to
BOM DocumentationReference { type?, package?, instance?, file?, url?, property?, aggregation?,
association?, capability?, relationFqn?, context, languageFqn? }. Optional relation attribute
references org.blockml.bml.relation.* — default org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso when omitted.
Optional language attribute overrides the effective natural language for the relationship
text body.

Nine mutually exclusive target attributes (type, package, instance, file, url, property, aggregation,
association, capability) instead of one generic target. Type targets use TypeReference;
package targets use PackageReference; instance targets use InstanceReference; member targets
declare a concrete kind — property : PropertyReference, aggregation : AggregationReference,
association : AssociationReference, capability : CapabilityReference — and store the
canonical definition path in the BOM (for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width).
Split authoring type="com.foo.Bar" property="width" resolves to that path — type qualifies
the member name and is not stored as a separate type target. Split authoring
type="com.foo.Bar" instance="myId" resolves to com.foo.Bar::myId.
The attribute name encodes the target kind at the read site — see type (TypeReference),
see package (PackageReference), see instance (InstanceReference), see property
(PropertyReference), see file (repository documentation), see url (web address). Humans and
LLMs classify each reference from element shape alone without inferring kind from value
syntax. See 02_mbml.md — Associations vs References · references — Why separate target
attributes.

Rectangle typeData for a port shape — SCAD [[width, height], roundingRadius].
FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.Port.PortRectShapeSettings.

Reserved: emitted when a call maps ambiguously under a custom FunctionMapping. Until custom
mappings ship, treat as reserved.
Reserved: emitted when a call maps ambiguously under a custom FunctionMapping.

Reserved: emitted when an implementation requires a non-default FunctionMapping but none
is declared. Until custom mappings ship, treat as reserved. Default FunctionMapping covers
V1 built-ins.
Reserved: emitted when an implementation requires a non-default FunctionMapping but none is declared.

Root Blocks must not declare <visibility>. Sub-Blocks inside <subBlocks> may declare optional visibility matching their name prefix.
Emitted when a document-root Block declares root-level visibility — only Sub-Blocks may do so.

Root semantic unit of BlockML — the sole inheritance root for all Block definitions.
Every concept in the grammar is a Block: composable domain types, ValueTypes, Languages,
Status values, Constraints, Capabilities, Exceptions, Services, Libraries, and Definition meta-model
types. Unqualified name Block resolves to this type.

Role and constraints:
• Sole inheritance root — omits <baseType>; all other definitions must declare a non-empty parent FQN
• Package org.blockml.bml.core — every root Block in this package must inherit directly from
  this type. Nested Sub-Blocks in core are exempt (doc:ModelingGuidelines)
• Abstract — not used directly as a composition instance type
• Further members defined by sub-types — Properties, Aggregations,
  Associations, and Capabilities via the baseType chain
• Composition instance identity uses bml:id and bml:version (not member attributes)
• Documentation prose language is Definition meta (def:BlockDefinition.language), not a
  member of this type — this document authors <language><English/></language> as the
  framework default for inheritance

Type reference rules:
• Aggregation member types may be any Block FQN
• Association member types must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[]
• Property and Capability payload types must resolve to a ValueType
• Capability throws lists Exception types via TypeReferenceEntity — not ValueType payloads
• Capability implementation language attributes reference org.blockml.bml.language.* — unqualified names permitted

Documentation model (on every root block definition — see def:BlockDefinition /
doc:DocumentationModel):
• Definition identity first — element type/name tag (preferred) or <name> / <type> /
  <baseType> (baseType omitted only here; dual format: doc:DocumentFormat)
• <is> — always required after identity; clear Urbild designation (what the Block semantically represents)
• <summary> — required when documentation is too long for a quick scan
• <language> — optional Definition meta; natural language for documentation prose
  (inherits from enclosing Library document, then this Block document's English default)
• <documentation> — always required; technical description; optional language
  attribute when prose deviates from effective block language
• <isNot> — required when confusion risk exists
• Optional extensions: <since>, <changelog>, <examples>, <references>
Omitted is or documentation → BML_MISSING_IS / BML_MISSING_DOCUMENTATION; missing isNot or
summary when required → BML_MISSING_IS_NOT / BML_MISSING_SUMMARY (warning V1).

Serialization:
• bml:xml ${ bml:Self } — composable instances render under their declared type tag
  (for example <core:Block>, <myns:Wall>)
• Definition branch types describe block structure and carry their own bml:xml rules

Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. Compatible with Integer, Float,
and Decimal properties. The value property must match T.

Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. Compatible with Integer, Float,
and Decimal properties. The value property must match T.

Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. The property value must be present
after all model resolution is complete — inheritance, contracts, default values, and instance
value binding. Only authored values count; expression evaluation does not satisfy ValuePresent
(Stage 2 does not evaluate expressions). Enforced by validateConstraints() at Stage 2 only when
validation references an understood Validation block (typically validation:Error). Declares no
own properties beyond the inherited validation reference.

Self-hosting bootstrap: the compiler loads framework BML from @blockml/core (and domain
packages) before user content — TypeRegistry bootstrap, not special-cased type semantics
in code.

Bootstrap order (summary):
1. Core branches — Block, ValueType, Language, Status, Relation, Constraint, Capability, Definition
2. Concrete types — Integer, Decimal, languages, services, constraints, relations
3. BlockLibrary — library descriptor base (readMe, bootstrap, dependencies, subLibraries)
4. org.blockml.bml.Library — published library; members by file location under Library.bml;
   readMe → README
5. Domain framework BML (e.g. com.machineblocks.bml.core.*)

Two library entry roles (do not conflate):
• org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe — human/LLM reading entry. Required on every Library via
  readMe (exactly one TypeReferenceEntity(ReadMe)). org.blockml.bml.README is the standard
  core-library ReadMe.
• org.blockml.bml.core.Bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (tasks, agents, CI). At most one
  per Library via bootstrap (0..1). Empty abstract branch; concrete subtypes supply process logic.

Concrete Library.bml <references> — at most two <see> entries on the catalog
descriptor (not on documentation blocks):
1. Required relation=ReadFirst → the ReadMe named in readMe
2. Optional relation=ThenContinueWith → the Bootstrap named in bootstrap (only when present)
Signals: after reading, continue by executing the automation SPOE. No AuthoringGuide /
DeepDive / Extends / SeeAlso on concrete Libraries.

Curated reading order lives in <references> on the ReadMe block — each entry uses
relation=ReadFirst with a context note. Available how-tos use relation=HowToIndex on the same
references container. One mechanism for all cross-links; tooling filters by relation. No
separate reading-order aggregation on ReadMe itself.

How-to paths:
• org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.HowTo — procedural org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.* blocks
• relation=HowToStep — ordered steps inside a HowTo (document order)
• relation=Prerequisite — before starting a how-to
• org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic — org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* validator codes
• relation=Resolves — Diagnostic → HowTo fix procedure

Interpretation context:
• Framework BML defines what types ARE — TypeRegistry SSOT
